text: New planet.New job.. “Welcome to Planet Ten! It’s your first day as an apprentice Block Manipulator.”. “I’m Mr. Martian. Head of training. Literally.”
Glowblocks™POWER OF TEN!. “Glowblocks™ capture the POWER OF TEN! Ten smaller units join to make one bigger unit. Same value. Bigger wobble.”
Meet yourrobot helper.. “TEN-BOT will help you aim, split and collect. We will check the value and count the blocks together.”. “Only the next action is unlocked. Take your time!”
Let’s see whatyou can do.. “Your job is to reshape deliveries so they fit the colony’s machines.”

I am TEN-BOT! One ten rod is worth 10, but it is ONE separate block. Value counts the glowing cells. Block count counts separate pieces. Type the total value and the number of blocks. Then choose Check my answers.
Choose the pink Discombobulator below. It splits a bigger block into smaller blocks.
Now aim at the glowing ten rod and click it once. Keyboard: Tab to Ten block 1, then press Enter.
You split one ten into ten separate ones. Count the value, then count the separate blocks. Nothing was added or lost. Type the total value and the number of blocks. Then choose Check my answers.
Choose the blue Transmorgifier below. It joins ten matching blocks into one bigger block.
Hold the mouse or your finger on the first one, sweep across all TEN ones, then release. Keyboard: Tab to each one and press Enter. If some fall back, try again!

Ten ones joined into one ten. The ten glowing cells still have the same value. How many separate blocks can you pick up now? Type the total value and the number of blocks. Then choose Check my answers.
New delivery! ONE ten and TWO ones. Count the ten as 10 for value, but as just ONE separate block. Now add the two ones. Type the total value and the number of blocks. Then choose Check my answers.
Training complete! VALUE is how much the blocks are worth. BLOCK COUNT is how many separate pieces there are. Splitting and joining change the count, but keep the value.
For VALUE, each ten rod is worth 10 and each one is worth 1. Count the glowing cells, not just the separate pieces. Try again.
The value is right! For BLOCKS, count each whole rod once and each separate one once. Try the block count again.
